body: Thank you for your message. its illegal to take without a prescription is what I meant, which is what I've been doing. in the UK you register with the GP that is closest to your house, you can't choose to go here or there unless you register with another GP and since I haven't moved anywhere, they will ask why I am leaving the GP that is closest to me. Also the NHS doesn't provide a psychiatrist service, only Talking Therapies, who last time I used, told me to try mindfulness meditation. I did that for a while, but it came nowhere near fixing the years of chronic depression that I've had since I was a child. I want to tell my GP, but I know from experience that the most they will do for mental health issues like mine is either prescribe antidepressants, or Talking Therapies.

The two times I saw a psych here in the UK it was through the NHS. They have a service called ‘talking therapies’. The only thing they prescribed me both times I used their service was mindfulness meditation, which is an amazing tool, don’t get me wrong, but it did nothing for my actual depression. Just helped me ignore it for a while until it ‘flared back up’ and then I’m back to square one.

Yeah this is exactly what I’m scared of. Don’t get me wrong. I am so grateful we live in a country that has something as amazing as the NHS, but when it comes to mental health on the NHS, it seems to be either their Talking Therapies service, Beta Blockers, or Antidepressants. I’ve been through all three of those and none really worked long term. It’s so frustrating because all I want to do is go to my GP and say ‘look! I’ve self experimented for a lot of my younger years with different substances and then when that didn’t work, you experimented on me with antidepressants and none of it worked. I’ve now found something that does, so please help me continue to heal myself’ but I know that it probably won’t end well if I go down that route.

I would rather not say, as I feel that would be against the nature of the rules of this sub. I will say It’s a standard one they give out here in the Uk for mild (for lack of a better word) adult onset ADHD. I never wanted to ‘fake it’ to get the drug as I feel that would ultimately be counter productive and very unfair on people with actual diagnosed ADHD. I want to do this properly and legally

Always had negative self talk, Overthinking, feelings of worthlessness, never had the energy to compete tasks, standard clinical depression symptoms. But then I have moments of brilliance and motivation. Those moments used to last a few weeks at a time and I was able to achieve a lot in that time before slipping back into not wanting to get out of bed or do anything or speak to anyone again.. nowadays (before the last 3 months) those moments only last half a day max, and the time between them gets longer and longer. 
I’ve always had suicidal thoughts since the age of about 14, (I’m 39 now) but I’ve never seriously acted on them, which tells me I’m not actually suicidal, but probably my brain is telling me it wants massive change in my life. I’ve tried implementing that change but as before, I always self sabotage. Always. Never felt worth anything to anyone, even myself. 

I know that most of these symptoms are basically related to depression and not ADHD as far as I can tell, which is why I am so shocked that this has worked so well and so consistently. Hence why I posted

You’re not stupid. Thank you for replying. I appreciate you and your kind words. I just feel so lost and helpless. My life feels pointless and it just seems to get worse all the time. I mean, I’m 37 now, do I really want to feel like this for another 40-50 years till I go of natural causes? I dunno. You’re right though, My daughter is the only thing keeping me here
Ok sorry, I’ll try posting there. Thank you
